subject: Intermittent 503s + tail-latency spikes — renewal path & premium SLA request
messages:
From: Claire Hughes <claire@atlasedge.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Repeated 503s and search tail latency — we need a commercial path

Diego / team,

Over the past week we've seen three incidents where our end users experienced 503s for short bursts (~2–5 minutes) and another set of longer tail-latency spikes (95th-99th) that doubled our median response time. This is hitting our primary search flows and directly affecting conversions.

We appreciate the on-call responses so far, but the recurrence has made the exec team nervous about the standard SLAs in our renewal window. We want to discuss a concrete upgrade path to the premium SLA (lower P95/P99 targets + credits for incidents) and a short dedicated pilot to validate mitigations before renewal.

Can we schedule a call next week? Also: please share any incident logs you can (we've attached a short summary).

Best,
Claire Hughes
Head of Product Operations
AtlasEdge

Attachments: atlasedge-incident-summary-20260815.pdf (attachment stub)

2) Engineering triage: I'll loop Markus to share logs and a first-pass mitigation plan.
3) Commercial path: Ben will outline what a Premium SLA addendum looks like (targets, credits, pilot conditions).

Markus — can you pull the request-level traces and the KV cache heatmap for the 15th? If you already have any preliminary root-cause notes, paste them into the thread.

Claire / Raj — I'll send a calendar invite now.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez

From: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Claire Hughes <claire@atlasedge.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2026 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Repeated 503s and search tail latency — we need a commercial path

Thanks for the ping. Quick notes from triage (incidents on 2026-08-13, 14, 15):

- Symptom: brief 503 bursts and elevated P95/P99 for sequences > 512 tokens on the search completion path.
- Observed trigger: sudden traffic waves causing KV cache churn and a small fraction of requests routed to a salvaged fallback model with longer cold-start latency.
- Root cause hypothesis: autoscaler thresholds + cache eviction policy interacted with a transient spike in a particular query cohort.

Immediate mitigations we've applied (already live):
- Raised autoscaler headroom for the search model pool (+20% buffer during peak windows).
- Turned on preferential affinity so hot KV cache shards stay warm for AtlasEdge sessions.
- Put a soft cap fallback route to a lower-latency quantized variant only for high-backlog windows.

Request for AtlasEdge techs: please share a sample of the user query blast pattern (we need ~30 mins of seq/latency distribution). I'll analyze and follow up with a recommended cache policy change and an optional canary-only dedicated pilot (2-week) on reserved instances to validate.

Estimate for a pilot + SLA addendum: engineering ~2 days to configure pilot & monitoring; legal/commercial ~3–5 business days for addendum review.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: technical-annotated-trace-snippet.txt (stub)

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Claire Hughes <claire@atlasedge.com>, Raj Patel <raj.p@atlasedge.com>, diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2026 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Commercial path: Premium SLA addendum & two-week dedicated pilot

Claire / Raj — following our call, here's the commercial outline we can take into renewal to address AtlasEdge's concerns: 

- Two-week dedicated pilot on reserved instances (pilot nodes isolated to AtlasEdge traffic). Objective: validate P95/P99 improvements during your peak windows.
- Premium SLA addendum (proposed terms): P95 < 150ms, P99 < 400ms for the search route, with rolling credits for incidents exceeding thresholds.
- One-time implementation credit: Redwood will waive the first month of premium surcharge if pilot demonstrates >30% reduction in tail-latency incidents.
- Timeline: pilot starts as soon as AtlasEdge signs the addendum; pilot monitoring dashboard will be shared.

Next steps for procurement: we'll upload a formal addendum doc and DocuSign link. Procurement, if you can review the attached draft (sla-draft-atlasedge-20260822.docx) and flag changes, we'll turn this around quickly.

Diego / Markus — any gating tech items on your side before we hand this to procurement?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-draft-atlasedge-20260822.docx (attachment stub)

From: Raj Patel <raj.p@atlasedge.com>
To: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, Claire Hughes <claire@atlasedge.com>
Cc: procurement@atlasedge.com, diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 16:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial path: Premium SLA addendum & two-week dedicated pilot

Ben / Diego — procurement reviewed the draft and is generally aligned. A few minor legal points (we'll mark them in the Docx) but nothing blocking. AtlasEdge is willing to start the two-week dedicated pilot as an addendum to our existing contract while legal finalizes wording — provided Redwood agrees to the pilot acceptance criteria below:

Pilot acceptance criteria (summary):
- Pilot must run during AtlasEdge peak window (07:00–11:00 PT daily) for 10 business days.
- Measured P95/P99 targets per the addendum thresholds.
- Redwood provides daily roll-up and a final evaluation report.
- If pilot meets >30% reduction in tail-latency incidents we move forward with premium upgrade; otherwise we revisit configuration.

Please send the DocuSign link and a final setup checklist for the pilot. We'll sign the addendum once the minor legal redlines are addressed in parallel.

Thanks — Raj
Raj Patel
VP Engineering (AtlasEdge)
